newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB debenture untraded after loan guarantee report.
newsitem.headline: NCB debenture untraded after loan guarantee report.

text.p: The five-year debenture issued by Nippon Credit Bank Ltd was untraded on Wednesday, as sentiment was dampened by a newspaper report saying that loan guarantees made by the bank for its financially troubled non-bank unit may affect the bank's business, a brokerage house trader said. A bank spokesman later denied the report.

Meanwhile, the yield of the new five-year bank debenture with a coupon of 1.8 percent issued in November by the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) slipped to 1.81 percent on Wednesday morning from Tuesday's 1.85 percent in the dealers' over-the-counter market in Tokyo.

The Asahi Shimbun said the bank issued a letter to agricultural financial institutions which had extended loans totalling 240 billion yen to the unit, Crown Leasing. In the letter, NCB said it would take responsibility for the unit's management.
The bank's spokesman said that while the bank had given a written statement, this did not mean it was guaranteeing the loans.
The fall in the yield of IBJ's debenture was largely due to a firmer Japanese government bond (JGB) market, the trader said. NCB's debenture was last traded at 2.35 percent on Tuesday, he said.
